meta.title: Felipe Laskos - Full Stack Developer
meta.description: Full stack developer based in Curitiba, Brazil. I build products, study technology and share what I learn along the way.

hero.tagline: I like to understand the problem before writing the code.
hero.pitch: I'm a full stack developer, passionate about technology and constant learning. I enjoy turning what I know into hands-on projects, exploring new technologies and understanding how the different parts of a system connect.

about.title: My journey in tech
about.p1: I got into software development in 2021, through Edutech. I started with front-end, went through Alura's program and, as I understood the field better, I realized I also wanted to know what was happening behind the scenes. That's where my interest in back-end, databases and architecture came from.
about.p2: Today I work as a full stack developer at Nex Energy, where I started as an intern and was brought on to stay. Day to day, I deal with real product problems: data, APIs, integrations, jobs, interfaces and technical decisions. I especially like to understand the context before touching the code, because a good solution starts long before the editor.

facts.focus: Full stack · Software architecture · Continuous learning

items.description: After almost a year as an intern, I was brought on to keep working on Nex's products. Today I take part in bigger problems and technical decisions, building everything from data models and APIs to interfaces and integrations.

This is where being a developer stopped being just a dream and became a real job. I shipped features to production, took part in code reviews and learned to work as a team on code that can't trade quality for "just working".
Before becoming a dev, I learned the essentials of working in any company. Organization, responsibility, communication and routine turned out to be just as important as technical skills.

projects.title: Things I've built along my tech journey
projects.intro: My personal projects are my laboratory. Not all of them were born to become products. Some were born simply because I wanted to find out how something worked.

doAndBuild.name: Do And Build
doAndBuild.description: A mix of productivity, learning and gamification. Users build study roadmaps, organize tasks into folders and construct a house as they make progress.
highlights: Full authentication with Spring Security and JWT
Public folders, likes and roadmap cloning
Progress turned into a house that grows with the user

podpatoFullstack.name: PodPato - Full Stack
podpatoFullstack.description: The project that started as a simple podcast aggregator and ended up becoming a complete web development exercise, with users, persistence, interaction and an evolving architecture.
highlights: Authentication and user accounts with Passport
Comments with a full create, edit and delete cycle
Saved videos and history persisted with MongoDB

podpatoFrontend.name: PodPato - Front-end
podpatoFrontend.description: The first version of PodPato and one of the projects that shaped my JavaScript learning phase. No framework, no unnecessary abstractions: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and the YouTube API.
highlights: Direct integration with the YouTube API
Saved videos and watch history persisted in the browser
An app built entirely with vanilla JavaScript

ticTacToe.name: Tic Tac Toe
ticTacToe.description: A small but intentional project. I used a simple game to practice React for real: components, state, effects and how different parts of the interface interact.
highlights: Players pick their symbol and nickname

writing.title: I write to consolidate and share knowledge
writing.lead: I really enjoy writing about technology. My texts usually come after going through a challenge, finishing a project or learning something new. I believe writing is not only a way to share, but also an excellent way to consolidate knowledge.
writing.medium: Texts about development, tools, architecture and things I've learned building software day to day.
writing.substack: A more personal space to talk about career, learning and the experience of building a path in technology.

contact.title: Got something to build?
contact.lead: If you want to talk about development, a project, technology or just exchange ideas, reach out. I enjoy good conversations as much as good problems to solve.

footer.built: Built with Next.js, Tailwind CSS and Motion
